findings_addressed.oracle: Python bitwise complement: bytes(b ^ 0xFF for b in [0xAA, 0xBB, 0xCC, 0xDD]) == bytes([0x55, 0x44, 0x33, 0x22])
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/bridges/hex_editor.py, change the 'not' transform_map entry from 'bit_invert' to 'xor_repeating' (or make _apply_arithmetic_fallback return the original data for 'not') — the read-back assertion actual_bytes == expected_bytes would then fail.

notes: G0131 was a no-assertion tautology (N8/N4): it only checked dict keys and known-injected values without verifying the bitwise NOT was actually applied to the bytes. Hardened by reading back 4 bytes after the NOT operation and asserting they equal the bitwise complement of the original 0xAA 0xBB 0xCC 0xDD input, computed independently as b ^ 0xFF. Also strengthened result['offset'] == 0 assertion to pin the metadata to the actual byte position.
